strengths: Clear and elegant core idea: partitioning tokens instead of masking is simple, intuitive, and well-motivated for avoiding wasted computation on MASK tokens
Strong empirical results on text: 5-5.5x latency/throughput improvements on OpenWebText with competitive or better generative perplexity; 1.95x PPL improvement on LM1B

Rigorous experimental methodology: fair baseline comparisons (MDLM reimplemented), careful ablations, FP64 precision controls, honest disentanglement of complementary masking effects, downstream task evaluation
Excellent reproducibility: detailed hyperparameters, code provided, clear algorithms, complete computational cost breakdown with training/inference analysis
Honest discussion of limitations: authors transparently acknowledge training overhead, performance-parameter tradeoffs, preliminary image results, and architectural design challenges
weaknesses: Limited conceptual novelty: primarily an architectural engineering trick rather than fundamental advance in generative modeling; partitioning is straightforward with minimal theoretical insight into why it works; specific to discrete diffusion models
Significant training cost overhead: PGMs train 25-32% slower than MDLM (Table 3), use inefficient dense attention masks, and total training cost undermines practical value of inference gains

Model size scaling complications: same-layer PGMs underperform MDLM on OpenWebText, requiring larger models (dim=1024 vs 768) for fair comparison; unclear why increased embedding helps and what this reveals about the approach

Weak cross-modal generalization: image results explicitly preliminary with less pronounced gains; no architecture optimization for images; unclear applicability beyond discrete diffusion models and text

Poor distillation performance: PGM+SDTT achieves higher perplexity than MDLM+SDTT after distillation (Figure 6, Table 7); worse entropy preservation; suggests architectural incompatibility with distillation methods

Incomplete mechanistic analysis: complementary masking helps on LM1B but not OWT with only speculative explanations; unclear decomposition of gains from partitioning vs. architecture vs. model size; gap between MDLM with complementary masking and PGM not explained

Training stability concerns: Figure 5 shows loss spikes with complementary masking; different precision requirements (BF16 vs FP32) with unclear causes; single-seed training without error bars on validation PPL

Ad-hoc architectural design: multiple GroupSwap variants tested; data-independent initialization surprisingly outperforms with unclear justification; no self-attention in decoder limits expressiveness; sensitivity to design choices without clear guidance

Limited scope of comparisons: only compared to MDLM; no other efficient non-autoregressive or discrete diffusion variants tested; generative perplexity metric is indirect; downstream improvements are modest and mixed

Narrow applicability: results limited to discrete diffusion models; unclear how approach generalizes to continuous diffusion, autoregressive models, or multimodal settings beyond preliminary image results

strengths: Novel partitioning approach that elegantly avoids explicit MASK tokens during inference
Strong inference speedups (5-5.5x latency/throughput) on OpenWebText text generation
Comprehensive experiments with good ablations on architecture choices and multiple datasets
Clear presentation with effective figures and reproducible setup with code provided
Careful experimental details and hyperparameter reporting enabling reproduction
weaknesses: Critical confound in main claims: speedup comparisons use larger PGM models; same-size PGM 6/6 underperforms MDLM (26.96 vs 25.35 PPL on OWT), making attribution of improvements unclear
Significant training efficiency overhead (75% throughput on OWT, 68% on ImageNet) buried in appendix despite being a major practical limitation; total cost not quantified
Distillation underperformance: MDLM+SDTT outperforms PGM+SDTT (36.08 vs 49.48 PPL), suggesting architectural incompatibility with existing acceleration methods

Limited scope: strong results only on text; image results acknowledged as preliminary with less pronounced gains; inconsistent complementary masking effects across datasets (helps LM1B, negligible on OWT)
Weak downstream task improvements (Table 4) with underperformance on some benchmarks, suggesting primary contribution is inference optimization rather than model quality
Incomplete effect decomposition: difficult to isolate whether gains come from partitioning, encoder-decoder architecture, complementary masking, or model size differences
No error bars on main results and single runs for expensive models, limiting confidence in observed differences
Insufficient baselines: no comparison with other discrete diffusion acceleration techniques or recent non-autoregressive methods

strengths: Novel and elegant core idea: partitioning tokens instead of masking is simple, intuitive, and eliminates inefficient MASK token processing during inference
Substantial and well-documented inference speedups: consistent 5-5.5x improvements in latency/throughput on OpenWebText across different step counts, with 10.73x vs GPT-2
Comprehensive experimental evaluation: multiple datasets, careful ablations disentangling complementary masking from architecture effects, investigation of context-length dependencies
Technically sound: correctly designed training objective with asymmetric weighting (Eq. 6), well-motivated architecture with clear design principles
Excellent reproducibility: detailed hyperparameters, open datasets, promise to release code, transparent discussion of computational costs
Strong empirical validation: reports both validation perplexity and generative perplexity, addresses numerical precision issues, includes entropy metrics to detect degenerate generation
weaknesses: Context-dependent performance: benefits vary significantly by dataset/sequence length (1.95 PPL improvement on LM1B-128, but requires larger models on OWT-1024), and complementary masking analysis doesn't fully explain these differences

Training cost trade-off inadequately addressed: PGM achieves only ~75% of MDLM training throughput on OWT (Table 3), but paper doesn't clearly discuss when inference gains justify higher training costs
Inferior distillation results: MDLM+SDTT achieves better generative perplexity than PGM+SDTT (Figure 6), indicating fundamental architectural limitations with existing distillation methods

Required architectural complexity: unlike training-only modifications, PGM requires encoder with group-wise attention, novel GroupSwap layer, and decoder without self-attention, limiting ease of adoption
Limited evaluation of text quality: no human evaluation of generation quality, reliance on generative perplexity (GPT-2 based) may not fully capture sample quality
Incomplete baseline comparisons: primarily compares to MDLM and GPT-2; Block Diffusion and other non-autoregressive methods mentioned but not compared
Image experiments preliminary: acknowledged by authors; results show less pronounced speedups for shorter sequences, limiting claims about generality across modalities
Single-seed experiments: acknowledged practical limitation but reduces confidence in perplexity claims, especially for small differences
Missing analysis: unexplained phenomena (why complementary masking helps LM1B but not OWT, why larger embeddings outperform more layers on OWT), no guidance on failure cases or when to prefer MDLM

strengths: Clear, well-motivated contribution addressing a real inefficiency in masked generative models through elegant partitioning mechanism instead of masking
Substantial and consistent practical speedups: 5-5.5× for language modeling, 7.5× for image generation, validated across multiple domains (text and vision)
Comprehensive experimental evaluation with proper baselines (MDLM, MaskGIT), thorough ablations including isolation of complementary masking effects, downstream task evaluation on 8 benchmarks
Well-designed Partition Transformer architecture with clear enforcement of partition independence constraints while enabling necessary information exchange via GroupSwap layer
Excellent reproducibility with detailed hyperparameters, sampling algorithms, comprehensive appendices, and promised MIT-licensed code release
Honest and transparent discussion of limitations including training overhead, parameter increases needed on OpenWebText, and inconsistent complementary masking benefits across datasets
weaknesses: Non-trivial unresolved training overhead: PGM achieves ~75% of MDLM's training throughput on OpenWebText (63 vs 81 seq/sec), limiting practical adoption during model development despite inference speedups
Parameter count inflation required for competitive performance on longer sequences: PGM needs 268M parameters vs MDLM's 170M to match performance on OpenWebText, complicating efficiency comparisons
Complementary masking benefits do not generalize consistently: strong gains on LM1B (1.95 PPL reduction) but negligible on OpenWebText (0.09 PPL), with incomplete analysis of why
Limited theoretical justification: no formal analysis of why partition-based training with independence constraints should match masking performance; intuitions lack rigor
Marginal downstream task improvements: six-of-eight benchmark improvements are small in magnitude, with some degradations (e.g., OpenBook QA: 26.60 vs 28.60), questioning practical downstream benefit
Image generation results less compelling than language modeling: 32-step PGM underperforms MaskGIT (5.54 vs 5.35 FID), requiring doubled steps to achieve better quality
Distillation strategy represents compromise: applying SDTT loss to only one partition while masking the other, with paper acknowledging this setup 'naturally favors MDLM'
Limited experimental scope: restricted to ImageNet256 and context lengths up to 1024, with ImageNet training budget (500k steps) less than baselines (2M steps)

strengths: Clear motivation for inference efficiency improvements in MGMs with straightforward partitioning solution
Comprehensive experiments across multiple modalities (text and images) with thorough ablations and supplementary analysis

Unfair experimental comparisons: models compared at different parameter counts; ImageNet trained for 500k steps vs 2M for baselines due to computational constraints
Distillation results diminish advantage: nucleus sampling reduces speedup from 5.3× to 4.6× and matches MDLM in Gen. PPL, with advantage mainly for lower-quality standard sampling
Incomplete analysis of why complementary masking helps LM1B but not OWT; data-independent queries perform as well as data-dependent (Table 5), suggesting incomplete optimization
Downstream task evaluation (Table 2) shows inconsistent improvements despite 58% more parameters; no statistical significance testing provided

strengths: Novel and well-motivated approach: partitioning instead of masking elegantly combines benefits of autoregressive (efficient sampling) and masked models (parallel generation)

Clear presentation and excellent figures effectively communicating core concepts
